# tag: science.physics.density
will ice float or sink | does ice sink in water | is ice denser than water => Yes, ice floats. It's about 0.92 g/cm³, a bit less dense than water, because water molecules spread out into an open pattern when they freeze. That's why about 90% of an iceberg is underwater.
does cork float | will cork float or sink | does cork sink in water | is cork denser than water => Yes, cork floats very well. It's only about 0.24 g/cm³ because it's full of tiny air-filled cells.
does balsa wood float | will balsa wood float or sink | does balsa wood sink in water | is balsa wood denser than water => Yes, balsa wood floats easily. It's one of the lightest woods, often around 0.1 to 0.2 g/cm³.
does wood float | will wood float or sink | is wood denser than water => Most wood floats because it's less dense than water, usually about 0.4 to 0.9 g/cm³. A few very dense woods, like ebony and lignum vitae, sink.
does ebony float | will ebony float or sink | does ebony sink in water | is ebony denser than water => Ebony usually sinks. It's around 1.1 to 1.2 g/cm³, denser than water, which is unusual for wood.
does aluminium float | will aluminium float or sink | does aluminium sink in water | is aluminium denser than water => A solid lump of aluminium sinks, since it's 2.7 g/cm³. A foil boat or a can can float, because its shape pushes aside enough water to hold it up.
does steel float | will steel float or sink | does steel sink in water | is steel denser than water => Solid steel sinks, since it's about 7.8 g/cm³. Steel ships float because their hollow shape pushes aside a weight of water equal to the ship's weight.
does gold float | will gold float or sink | does gold sink in water | is gold denser than water => Gold sinks fast. At about 19.3 g/cm³, it's over 19 times denser than water, which is why gold panners can wash lighter sand away and keep the gold.
does lead float | will lead float or sink | does lead sink in water | is lead denser than water => Lead sinks. It's about 11.3 g/cm³, which is why it's used for fishing weights and diving belts.
does glass float | will glass float or sink | does glass sink in water | is glass denser than water => Solid glass sinks, since it's about 2.5 g/cm³. An empty, sealed glass bottle can float because of the air inside it.
does pumice float | will pumice float or sink | does pumice sink in water | is pumice denser than water => Yes, pumice can float. This volcanic rock is full of gas bubbles, so it's less dense than water until water slowly soaks into the holes.
does granite float | will granite float or sink | does granite sink in water | is granite denser than water => Granite sinks. It's about 2.7 g/cm³, nearly three times as dense as water.
does a diamond float | will a diamond float or sink | does a diamond sink in water | do diamonds float => A diamond sinks. It's about 3.5 g/cm³.
will oil float or sink | does oil sink in water | is oil denser than water => Yes, cooking oil floats on water. It's about 0.92 g/cm³ and doesn't mix with water, so it forms a layer on top.
does honey float | will honey float or sink | does honey sink in water | is honey denser than water => Honey sinks in water. It's about 1.4 g/cm³, so it settles to the bottom of a glass before slowly dissolving.
does gasoline float | will gasoline float or sink | does gasoline sink in water | is gasoline denser than water => Gasoline floats on water, since it's about 0.7 to 0.77 g/cm³ and doesn't mix with water. That's one reason water is a bad way to put out a fuel fire.
does a candle float | will a candle float or sink | does a candle sink in water | do candles float => Yes, a wax candle floats. Paraffin wax is about 0.9 g/cm³, a little less dense than water.
will an apple float or sink | does an apple sink in water => Yes, apples float. About a quarter of an apple is air, so it's less dense than water. That's why bobbing for apples works.
does an orange float | will an orange float or sink | does an orange sink in water | do oranges float => An orange with its peel floats, because the peel is full of tiny air pockets like a life jacket. Peel it and the orange usually sinks.
does an egg float | will an egg float or sink | does an egg sink in water | do eggs float => A fresh egg sinks in water. As an egg ages, its air cell gets bigger, so an old egg stands up or floats. In very salty water, even a fresh egg floats.
does a grape float | will a grape float or sink | does a grape sink in water | do grapes float => Grapes usually sink in plain water because they're a bit denser than water. Raisins also sink at first.
does a potato float | will a potato float or sink | does a potato sink in water | do potatoes float => A potato usually sinks in plain water. It floats in very salty water, which is a fun density experiment.
does a coconut float | will a coconut float or sink | does a coconut sink in water | do coconuts float => Yes, coconuts float, thanks to their light, fibrous husk full of air. They can drift across oceans and grow on new beaches.
does a banana float | will a banana float or sink | does a banana sink in water | do bananas float => A banana usually floats, because it's slightly less dense than water.
does plastic float | will plastic float or sink | does plastic sink in water | is plastic denser than water => It depends on the plastic. Polyethylene and polypropylene, used in milk jugs and bottle caps, are less dense than water and float. PET drink bottles and PVC are denser and sink unless air is trapped inside.
does styrofoam float | will styrofoam float or sink | does styrofoam sink in water | is styrofoam denser than water => Yes, foam polystyrene floats very well because it's mostly air. Solid polystyrene, like in a plastic cup, is only just denser than water.
does a brick float | will a brick float or sink | does a brick sink in water | do bricks float => A brick sinks. Most are around 1.8 to 2 g/cm³.
does a person float | will a person float or sink | does a person sink in water | do people float => Most people can float, especially with lungs full of air. The body's density is very close to water's. Body fat floats, while bone and muscle sink, and salty sea water makes floating easier.
does mercury float | will mercury float or sink | does mercury sink in water | is mercury denser than water => Liquid mercury sinks under water, since it's about 13.5 g/cm³. It's so dense that a steel bolt floats on top of mercury.
does milk float | will milk float or sink | does milk sink in water | is milk denser than water => Milk is slightly denser than water, about 1.03 g/cm³, so it doesn't float on water. It mixes in instead.
# tag: science.physics.sound
how fast does sound travel in air | speed of sound in air | how fast is sound in air => Sound travels through air at about 343 m/s at 20 °C. It's a little faster in warm air and slower in cold air.
speed of sound in water | how fast is sound in water => Sound travels through water at about 1,480 m/s. That's over four times faster than in air.
how fast does sound travel in sea water | speed of sound in sea water | how fast is sound in sea water => Sound travels through sea water at about 1,500 m/s. It changes a bit with temperature, saltiness and depth.
how fast does sound travel in steel | speed of sound in steel | how fast is sound in steel => Sound travels through steel at about 5,000 to 6,000 m/s. That's up to about 17 times faster than in air, which is why you can hear a train coming through the rails before you hear it in the air.
how fast does sound travel in helium | speed of sound in helium | how fast is sound in helium => Sound travels through helium at about 1,000 m/s. That's why breathing helium makes your voice sound squeaky: the sound resonates at higher frequencies in your throat.
how fast does sound travel in ice | speed of sound in ice | how fast is sound in ice => Sound travels through ice at about 3,800 m/s. That's more than 10 times faster than in air.
how fast does sound travel in space | speed of sound in space | how fast is sound in space => Sound can't travel through space at all, because there's almost no matter there to carry the vibrations. Astronauts talk by radio, which uses light-speed radio waves.
# tag: science.chem.matter
what is the boiling point of ethanol | what is the melting point of ethanol | at what temperature does ethanol boil | at what temperature does ethanol melt => At normal air pressure, ethanol melts at about minus 114 °C and boils at about 78 °C. That's why alcohol evaporates faster than water and is used in thermometers for very cold places.
what is the boiling point of table salt | what is the melting point of table salt | at what temperature does table salt boil | at what temperature does table salt melt => At normal air pressure, table salt melts at about 801 °C and boils at about 1,465 °C.
what is the boiling point of ammonia | what is the melting point of ammonia | at what temperature does ammonia boil | at what temperature does ammonia melt => At normal air pressure, ammonia melts at about minus 78 °C and boils at about minus 33 °C. So it's a gas at room temperature, though it's sold dissolved in water as a cleaner.
what is the boiling point of methane | what is the melting point of methane | at what temperature does methane boil | at what temperature does methane melt => At normal air pressure, methane melts at about minus 182 °C and boils at about minus 162 °C. Natural gas, which is mostly methane, is shipped cooled to a liquid.
what is the boiling point of propane | what is the melting point of propane | at what temperature does propane boil | at what temperature does propane melt => At normal air pressure, propane melts at about minus 188 °C and boils at about minus 42 °C. It's stored as a liquid under pressure in barbecue tanks.
what is the boiling point of butane | what is the melting point of butane | at what temperature does butane boil | at what temperature does butane melt => At normal air pressure, butane melts at about minus 138 °C and boils at just below 0 °C. That's why lighters and camping stoves can struggle on freezing days.
what is the boiling point of acetone | what is the melting point of acetone | at what temperature does acetone boil | at what temperature does acetone melt => At normal air pressure, acetone melts at about minus 95 °C and boils at about 56 °C. Acetone is the main liquid in many nail polish removers.
what is the boiling point of liquid nitrogen | what is the melting point of liquid nitrogen | at what temperature does liquid nitrogen boil | at what temperature does liquid nitrogen melt => At normal air pressure, liquid nitrogen melts at about minus 210 °C and boils at about minus 196 °C. That's why liquid nitrogen boils wildly at room temperature.
what is the boiling point of liquid oxygen | what is the melting point of liquid oxygen | at what temperature does liquid oxygen boil | at what temperature does liquid oxygen melt => At normal air pressure, liquid oxygen melts at about minus 218 °C and boils at about minus 183 °C. Liquid oxygen is pale blue and is used in rockets to help the fuel burn.
what is the boiling point of glycerol | what is the melting point of glycerol | at what temperature does glycerol boil | at what temperature does glycerol melt => At normal air pressure, glycerol melts at about 18 °C and boils at about 290 °C. It's a thick, sweet liquid used in soap and bubble mixtures.
